newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian dlr ends firmer following Ontario budget.
newsitem.headline: Canadian dlr ends firmer following Ontario budget.

text.p: * Canada's dollar ended slightly firmer on Tuesday from Monday, closing at C$1.3782 (US$0.7256). * Positive news in Ontario budget was widely priced in and had little immediate impact on the currency, dealers said. * The market continued to benefit from expectations that pressure on the U.S. Federal Reserve to tighten rates had declined.
Canada's dollar ended slightly firmer in moderate trade on Tuesday, strengthening to C$1.3782 (US$0.7256) from Monday's close.
Dealers said the day's most significant event, the presentation of Ontario's fiscal 1997/98 budget, was in line with expectations and had little immediate impact on prices.

"Basically he (Ontario Finance Minister Ernie Eves) delivered what was expected, so the Canadian dollar again had a good day," said Stephen Wateridge, managing director of corporate foreign exchange at CIBC Wood Gundy Inc.

The Ontario government on Tuesday revised its deficit projection for the 1996-97 fiscal year to C$7.5 billion from C$7.67 billion and repeated its projection of a balanced budget by year 2000-01. Ontario is Canada's most populous and economically powerful province.
Analysts said the focus for the Canadian market was now shifted to the question of whether or not the U.S. Federal Reserve would hike interest rates when the Open Market Committee met on May 20.

"As fears of a May 20 Fed rate hike subside it looks as though the Bank of Canada has won the battle over domestic interest rates," Technical Data market analyst Jeoff Hall said in a commentary. "That allowed the Canadian dollar some room to maneuver Tuesday."
On the crosses, the Canadian dollar softened to 1.2492 marks from Monday's close of 1.2563 and dipped to 90.95 yen from Monday's 91.72 yen.
